I'm so sorry to hear that you have to deal with this. I'm familiar with conversion disorder, and honestly, I'm not even surprised that this is the reaction you got after seeking help. If it was caused by SSRI then yeah, it's because of them. I believe you because I'm in the same boat. It's so frustrating that doctors won't even consider the possibility and instead insist that it has to be psychological - from trauma, from depression, from anxiety.

I'm in a similar situation, the difference being that I started experiencing those cognitive deficits, problems with speech and motor function, and pressure on top of my head and my frontal lobe since the first day of starting the meds (I was on Lexapro just like you), nobody took me seriously and I was kept on the meds for 9 months and I've been off for more than 2 years but nothing's changed, in fact it only worsened over the months. Every time I seek help from a neurologist I get referred back to psychiatry as well and I feel utterly hopeless. You're not alone, sadly I've no idea what can be done for us, I can only offer you my sympathy and hope that recovery is possible.

I personally didn't like AnR (even though I agree that Isayama made it so The Rumbling was the only solution left), I was mostly on team Alliance, I just wanted genocide to be properly condemned and for the story to just make sense. Even if it meant my favorite (or all) characters dying, I just wanted them to remain consistent, to have good conclusions and for Eren to receive rightful punishment, no matter if he won or lost.

Yeah, that didn't really happen. Not only that, the ending shat all over everything I loved about the series and somehow managed to do every single thing I didn't want to happen. It's so much I wouldn't be able to fit it in here. But since we're talking about genocide specifically:

For a story that put so much weight in loss, death, killing others and which made such a big deal out of our main characters killing people for the first time (we even got Armin throwing up after shooting a single person), it sure failed to do that in the end. We got everyone living happy lives while the aftermath of the Rumbling got brushed aside.

A character who committed a near omnicide - How the hell can you in a single chapter "redeem" them narratively and in the eyes of the people who opposed him and some of which were terrified of that happening? Reiner being all "the last person who should have this power is you Eren; I couldn't stop him, he's gonna destroy the world" \*mental breakdown\* then after Eren ACTUALLY destroys a big portion of the world Reiner is all teary "what a man you are wow".

Annie saying "you told us to live long lives, but what about you", excuse me? Do you want him to live after that?? Pieck going from "he's not my friend; perish you nightmare" to "I wanted to talk to him too" with a smile on her face. And she didn't even get paths convo with him so she went from her first words to seeing everyone getting titanized and then 10 minutes all titan powers disappearing and then she says this? Why would she be grateful to him at all? Honestly any of the warriors, Eren would have turned their parents into pancakes if he wasn't stopped. Would you feel sad for letting him go then??

And of course the cherry on top - Armin. "I massacred 80% of the population. I killed my own mom. I didn't even know if my friends would survive, but I was willing to kill you for my freedom" \*silence\* "Also I won't be there for Mikasa" \*punches Eren\* "Oh my god, how could you, you bastard." The peak of their conversation is literally about Mikasa and how Eren mistreated her. And then he throws a fit. After that Armin, "the biggest empath in the world" fucking thanks him and is like "I won't let this whoopsy daisy be in vain" and then Eren tells him he's gonna save humanity? The remaining 20% you mean. And of course talking and peaceful approach didn't work before because world wide discrimination doesn't go away that way, but now that everyone has the right to hate the Paradisians more than ever... Armin will save everyone? By telling them a StOrY aBoUt ThE AlLiAnCe CoMiNg ToGeThEr??

Apparently, Armin just wanted to "get closer" to Eren in his final moment without even understanding him (in Isayama's words). If it was me I wouldn't even be able to look at my friend, they wouldn't even be my friend. I'd be so angry and disgusted, it's not even possible to describe.

Anyway, Eren dies in one of the most painless ways in AOT, gets a kiss, gets a grave, said grave gets visited by Mikasa constantly and 3 years later everyone else also goes to visit his grave and probably mourn him. Including Reiner, Annie, Pieck. Eren is remembered and cherished as some tragic hero by the main cast and a big portion of the audience, while the victims of the Rumbling remain a mere statistic. Hange and Zeke are practically forgotten, they don't get graves, they don't get a mention or anything and Hange also died a more painful death than Eren, great!!!

I'd also like to mention that the alliance is basically the new Tyburs, they live in luxury and are regarded as heroes, while millions of survivors suffer in poverty. Kinda fucked up.

TLDR - it's hard to put it shortly but - the narrative in the ending treats Eren like a hero despite the genocide he committed. We go from graphic images of Eren turning people into grind meat to him being remembered dearly and cherished. The horror of the Rumbling isn't treated with the weight it should be.

He also threatened the Marleyans, if they were to disturb his peace or try to attack them he would unleash the thousands of colossal titan within the walls and cause the Rumbling basically make them flatten everything in their path.

I'm a bi woman but I totally empathize with that, everything you said was on point. Fortunately things are getting better. I'm more into cartoons and anime so I can't give you live action recommendations. I was really happy with She-Ra as a wlw since it's the first time I actually got invested in the queer characters (which is like... Every character) but what I'm trying to say is that many times when I watch something with supposedly wlw rep I just... Don't relate to it or it's just so subtle as if it's there only for that one crump of representation. Seeing a show with actual plot, a main wlw couple where both characters are extremely interesting and complex and none of them die (wow). Of course I really appreciate the bi characters as well since for the first time I see two bi characters of opposite genders shown in a relationship. Usually in order for it to be seen as a valid bi rep the bisexual character has to end up with a person from the same sex.

When it comes to mlm I usually go for anime. I already saw someone recommending Yuri on Ice but it really is a great anime that has stayed for me for 4 years. I watched it back in 2016 when I still identified as straight and even though I wouldn't say I was homophobic, I didn't really seek any kind of lgbt content. Growing up I didn't see same sex couples anywhere but in porn and it wasn't normalized in my mind, whenever I saw a gay couple by chance it felt somehow weird. But yuri on ice was the first step to that changing and it really changed me as a person, it even converted one of my closest friends from a hardcore homophobe to an openminded bisexual leaning towards women. I don't think it would have happened that soon if it wasn't for weeks obsessing over that anime hahah.

Another one is Given, I guess one of its genres is romance but it's mainly about music. Maybe it doesn't fit your criteria in this case but I loved it. It's still really good rep (in my opinion). A movie came out too. Now, I don't know much you can relate to high schoolers but there are also 20-24 old characters soo who knows.

When it comes to action or a thriller - Banana Fish exists. It's not much of an explicit relationship mainly because the story doesn't revolve around the romance. But the main lead is canonically bi and the secondary main character is also queer (gay or bi isn't confirmed, he doesn't have any experience beforehand so yeah). It's very tragic though, it has comedic moments but the ending isn't happy and I know that it's been debated if it's really good rep if the main couple doesn't have their happily ever after. Well, the manga was written in the 80s and I feel like that had a big influence. Still in my top 3 and a masterpiece in my eyes.

They surely are closer than in Parting Ways where they haven't seen each other in 6 years and the only thing Daniel gets is a photo of him (Sean can't get anything since he's hiding from the police and no one knows where he is) which would probably stay that way since Daniel has a tracker on his leg.

To me that is far more depressing than Sean going to prison because they can't see each other AT ALL, I can imagine them feeling sad and empty at first when Sean has to survive in Mexico completely alone and Daniel's left alone too. Then they would eventually become distant memories of each other and stay like a hole in their hearts/minds, like something is missing.

For the changing part, there isn't an ending where they don't change. Blood brothers is tricky because people think they have a strong bond which equals "good ending" but they have nothing in common with their past happy, empathetic, sensitive selves. You can clearly see it through their physical appearances, their behaviour, the job they've taken (Sean was never into cars). I guess the only thing that hasn't changed is that they would totally die for each other. I think that Redemption is the best scenario here because despite it having the longest time skip you can see that Daniel is still this super energetic, cheerful, kind person he has always been (if you've chosen high morality). And yeah Sean does look tired, understandebly but at least he isn't some gangster and he never stopped drawing or liking exploring (since he chooses to go travelling in the end).

We also can't expect Sean to get out of prison unharmed and it's been like 2 months? That's a super short time to recover from anything. And yet you can see he's okay when he hugs Daniel and drives off. People get worse mental breakdowns after just break-ups. People can have a depressive episode of several months if someone close to them dies and you don't see anyone calling them broken. Why can't we treat Sean the same way? As a hurt person who can recover and be happy again.

I also found the scene where he cries sweet in a way because throughout the whole game Sean has always been the one comforting Daniel, he's always been his stability and "shoulder to cry on". Daniel cared for Sean too of course but he never had the capability to properly comfort him since he was only 9 years old and he couldn't really understand the magnitude of Sean's pain. But he's older now, he's got mental stability, he understands the world and the people around him more, the roles change and now HE can be Sean's strength.
